hints.title: Two-Tier CTE Structuring
hints.text: Separate global customer metrics like totals and loyalty score from category frequency ranking to avoid aggregation conflicts.

hints.title: Top Category Tie-Breaking
hints.text: Use row number partitioned by customer ordered by category count descending and earliest transaction date ascending to pick the primary category.

hints.title: Loyalty Score Formula
hints.text: Combine transaction count multiplied by ten plus total spend divided by one hundred rounded to two decimal places.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH customer_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        t.customer_id,
        ROUND(SUM(t.amount), 2) AS total_amount,
        COUNT(t.transaction_id) AS transaction_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS unique_categories,
        ROUND(AVG(t.amount), 2) AS avg_transaction_amount,
        ROUND((COUNT(t.transaction_id) * 10) + (SUM(t.amount) / 100), 2) AS loyalty_score
    FROM Transactions t
    JOIN Products p ON t.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY t.customer_id
),
category_frequency AS (
    SELECT
        t.customer_id,
        p.category,
        COUNT(t.transaction_id) AS cat_count,
        MIN(t.transaction_date) AS earliest_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY t.customer_id
            ORDER BY COUNT(t.transaction_id) DESC, MIN(t.transaction_date) ASC
        ) AS rn
    FROM Transactions t
    JOIN Products p ON t.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY t.customer_id, p.category
)
SELECT
    m.customer_id,
    m.total_amount,
    m.transaction_count,
    m.unique_categories,
    m.avg_transaction_amount,
    c.category AS top_category,
    m.loyalty_score
FROM customer_metrics m
JOIN category_frequency c ON m.customer_id = c.customer_id AND c.rn = 1
ORDER BY m.loyalty_score DESC, m.customer_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Grouping by customer and category followed by window partitioning.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per customer incur repetitive full table scans.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Modular CTE execution enables single indexed joins.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applies window partition ranking for deterministic mode selection.

import pandas as pd

def analyze_customer_purchasing(transactions: pd.DataFrame, products: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if transactions.empty or products.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=[
            'customer_id', 'total_amount', 'transaction_count',
            'unique_categories', 'avg_transaction_amount', 'top_category', 'loyalty_score'
        ])
    
    df = transactions.merge(products, on='product_id', how='inner')
    
    # 1. Customer level aggregations
    grouped = df.groupby('customer_id')
    metrics = grouped.agg(
        total_amount=('amount', 'sum'),
        transaction_count=('transaction_id', 'count'),
        unique_categories=('category', 'nunique'),
        avg_transaction_amount=('amount', 'mean')
    ).reset_index()
    
    metrics['total_amount'] = metrics['total_amount'].round(2)
    metrics['avg_transaction_amount'] = metrics['avg_transaction_amount'].round(2)
    metrics['loyalty_score'] = ((metrics['transaction_count'] * 10) + (metrics['total_amount'] / 100)).round(2)
    
    # 2. Top category per customer
    cat_df = df.groupby(['customer_id', 'category']).agg(
        cat_count=('transaction_id', 'count'),
        earliest_date=('transaction_date', 'min')
    ).reset_index()
    
    cat_df = cat_df.sort_values(by=['customer_id', 'cat_count', 'earliest_date'], ascending=[True, False, True])
    top_cats = cat_df.drop_duplicates(subset=['customer_id'], keep='first')[['customer_id', 'category']]
    top_cats.rename(columns={'category': 'top_category'}, inplace=True)
    
    result = metrics.merge(top_cats, on='customer_id')
    result = result[[
        'customer_id', 'total_amount', 'transaction_count',
        'unique_categories', 'avg_transaction_amount', 'top_category', 'loyalty_score'
    ]]
    return result.sort_values(by=['loyalty_score', 'customer_id'], ascending=[False, True])
